title: customer-signal-gardener-rundown-and-sprint-seeds-2028-03-15
content:
Purpose: quick working digest of recent field signals (Feb 20–Mar 10 2028) + a short list of small experiments ("seeds") we can plant in the next 2 sprints to validate impact. Use this as a lightweight handoff to Product/Optimize/Infra for fast wins.

High-level snapshot
- Source mix: 60% support tickets + field calls, 25% in-product usage telemetry, 15% partner integration notes (marketplace/on-prem).
- Top themes: latency spikes at burst, unpredictable per-token cost for multi-tenant workloads, rollout pain for model variants, lack of quick knob for batching/caching tradeoffs in Console, requests for token-level billing visibility to reconcile costs.
- Severity split: 40% low-friction asks (UX/perf tweaks), 35% medium (ops/configuration/console affordances), 25% high (SLA complaints, private deploy onboarding blockers).

Representative customer lines (verbatim/scrubbed)
- "We see huge jitter whenever we get a campaign spike — p50 OK but p95 doubles and kills our UX." — mid-market SaaS company (embedded chat).
- "Our finance team can't reconcile the bill because embeddings + generations show as one line item; need per-route breakdowns." — e-comm enterprise.
- "Trying to do canary + A/B of quantized model is a nightmare — images/docs are different quality.": customer success note.

Signal clusters and quick interpretation
1) Burst latency & p95 jitter
   - Sources: time-windowed telemetry + 6 field reports. Patterns point to small bursts with identical sequence length distribution that trigger serialization/backpressure in a small cluster.
   - Hypothesis: autoscale and batching policy thresholds are too coarse for their traffic profile; KV cache warmup also contributes.
   - Customer impact: visible UX regressions and perceived reliability loss during campaigns.

2) Billing granularity for complex pipelines
   - Sources: 12 support threads, 3 renewal negotiation calls. Customers run mixed pipelines: embed -> rerank -> generate. Bills conflate token types; finance teams want per-step cost attribution and historical per-route totals for reconciliation.
   - Hypothesis: Console/usage pipeline attribution exists but is not exposed at token-level granularity or not easily exportable to finance tools.

3) Rollout/variant friction for private/dedicated users
   - Sources: 5 partner integration notes, 2 SRE escalations. Customers want safe canaries across model quantization levels or region fallbacks. Current rollout tools are powerful but lack simple preset templates for common patterns (canary percent + fallback).

4) Quality regressions post-quantization
   - Source: 7 eval regressions flagged by beta customers. They accept tradeoffs for cost but want deterministic diffs and tooling to compare outputs at scale.

Micro-probe candidates (seeds) — prioritized for ~2-week cycles
Note: choose small, measurable probes that reduce risk/answer customer questions. Each has an owner (CS-led) and a suggested success metric.

A) "Burst watcher" telemetry slice (owner: Samir Khan, effort: 3 dev-days)
  - What: add a telemetry view that surfaces p50/p95/p99 pre- and post-cache for requests that exceed X rps for 60s. Tag by customer, route, and model.
  - Why: quickly confirm whether jitter correlates to batching/backpressure or cache cold starts.
  - Success metric: identify top 5 offending routes for 3 pilot customers and reduce p95 by 25% via config change.

B) Billing mini-export for pipelines (owner: Arjun Patel, effort: 2 dev-days + 1 analytics-day)
  - What: CSV export from Console that breaks a selected date range into per-route/per-step token and cost estimates (embed/rerank/generate).
  - Why: addresses immediate finance reconciliation asks and reduces CS escalations during renewals.
  - Success metric: used by finance team in 2 customers during renewal; 80% reduction in clarification threads for invoice lines.

C) Canary template presets (owner: Product-Hosted API team, liaison: Maya Chen, effort: 5 dev-days + UX)
  - What: add 3 templates to Rollouts: (1) light-canary (5% traffic, 2m), (2) decaying-canary (10% -> 1% over 10m), (3) quantization-fallback (route to lower-cost model on quality regression).
  - Why: lowers friction for customers who want safe model experiments without writing custom rollout config.
  - Success metric: 3 pilot customers create a rollout using templates within 2 weeks; measured rollback rate and satisfaction.

D) Quantization diff harness (owner: Applied ML, liaison: CS, effort: 2 weeks medium)
  - What: a lightweight eval harness that runs a customer's sample prompts through two model variants and produces diff buckets (exact match, semantic shift, hallucination risk flags).
  - Why: reduces fear of quality regressions and enables informed cost/quality tradeoffs.
  - Success metric: pilot with 2 customers, measurable acceptance threshold (e.g., <2% high-impact diffs).

Quick operational patches (low cost)
- Console: expose route-level token estimates on the route details page (2 dev-days).
- Support: standardized invoice FAQ doc + sample CSV template for finance (owned by CS, 1 day).
- SRE runbook tweak: add explicit knob to temporarily increase batching-timeout for customers reporting p95 spikes (documented in SRE runbook).

Dependencies & blockers
- Access to per-request logs (privacy controls) — need Legal signoff to provide deeper traces to CS; pending legal review (ticket: JIRA-3120).
- Small infra work to expose pre- and post-cache timing in aggregated telemetry (infra ETA 2 sprints).

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: Billing export could confuse customers if cost estimation differs from invoice lines (currency conversion, credits). Mitigation: label as "estimate for reconciliation" and include link to billing team contact.
- Risk: Canary templates may create expectations for SLA guarantees. Mitigation: explicit copy in UI, and tie template to rollout guardrails (auto-fallback on error rate).

Open questions for Product/Infra/Applied ML
1) What is the minimum privacy-safe trace we can surface to CS without exposing raw customer prompts? (options: hashed prompts, token counts, hashed prompt fingerprints)
2) Can infra prioritize a telemetry slice for burst p95 within next 2 sprints? If not, what is the realistic ETA?
3) Applied ML: can we deliver a quant-diff prototype that runs on sampled customer prompts in <2 weeks? Needs compute budget and data access permission.

Suggested next steps (immediate)
- CS: schedule a 30-min sync with Product-Hosted API + Infra to review seeds and owners (target: Mar 18).
- Product: scope Canary template UX and wireframe quick copy by Mar 22.
- Infra: give ETA on telemetry slice by Mar 20.
- Applied ML: confirm compute + data permissions and whether a small N=200 prompt run is acceptable.

Notes to self (scratch)
- Follow-up with finance on sample invoice they used in Feb renewal (ask for CSV).
- Slack thread: #cs-field-notes — add summary post after triage.
- If telemetry probe shows KV cache warmup is >30% of p95, propose a short-term "cache pre-warm" opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Appendix: raw short snippets from tickets (redacted)
- "p95 jumps from 350ms -> 1.2s whenever marketing pushes a campaign; we have region failover but still see bad UX" (ticket 88721).
- "We can't map embeddings calls to the project that triggers them; bill shows one line for both embed and text generation" (ticket 89105).
- "Tried to roll out quantized-small model; generation quality dropped for multi-turn flows" (ticket 89330).

End — signoff: Maya C. (CS) — will update after product sync and infra ETA.
